q: When light is incident on the surface of an object some of the light is sent back and this phenomenon is called reflection of light.
e: True. When light is incident on the surface of an object some of the light is sent back and this phenomenon is called reflection of light. On reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

q: A ray of light is a path along which the light travels.
e: True. A ray of light is a path along which the light travels. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

q: A ray is represented by a straight line with an arrow-head pointing in the opposite direction of propagation of light.
e: False. A ray's arrow points in the direction the light is going, not against it.

q: A beam of light is a collection of rays of light.
e: True. A beam of light is a collection of rays of light. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: Searchlights used in trains and lighthouses emit a divergent beam of light.
e: False. Searchlights and lighthouses send a parallel or convergent beam so the light carries far, not a spreading divergent beam.

q: A parallel beam of light becomes a convergent beam after passing through a convex lens.
e: True. A parallel beam of light becomes a convergent beam after passing through a convex lens. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: A beam emitted by a light bulb is a divergent beam.
e: True. A beam emitted by a light bulb is a divergent beam. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: A line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence is called normal.
e: True. A line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence is called normal. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: An angle between the incident ray and the normal is an angle of reflection.
e: False. An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an angle of reflection. This claim used incident in place of reflected.

q: An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an angle of reflection.
e: True. An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an angle of reflection. An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an angle of reflection is light bouncing back from a surface.

q: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.
e: True. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane. The reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane is lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
e: True. The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection is light bouncing back from a surface.

q: Laws of reflection are true only for plane mirrors, not for curved mirrors.
e: False. The laws of reflection hold for curved mirrors as well as plane mirrors. On reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
